question: Should photoscrawl support arbitrary OpenAI-compatible image endpoints and a caller-facing per-asset export command in this PR, or should the change be narrowed to loopback LM Studio classification?
rationale: Repository policy requires an explicit privacy boundary for media leaving the machine and read-only treatment of Photos libraries; source inspection cannot decide whether maintainers intend to broaden either boundary or include the unrelated export surface.

options.title: Narrow and harden
options.body: Keep only LM Studio/OpenAI-compatible classification, default to loopback, add explicit remote opt-in and transmission provenance, and move export to a separate proposal.

options.title: Approve both surfaces
options.body: Retain remote endpoints and export only after adding explicit disclosure/provenance plus canonical rejection of every destination inside a Photos library package.

options.title: Pause this branch
options.body: Close or defer the draft and request separate focused PRs once endpoint policy and export scope are confirmed.

recommendation.title: Narrow and harden
recommendation.body: Keep only LM Studio/OpenAI-compatible classification, default to loopback, add explicit remote opt-in and transmission provenance, and move export to a separate proposal.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository policy names Josh as the source of current product direction, and this choice changes privacy and command-surface boundaries rather than only implementation details.
